name: Node/TypeScript with ESLint and Webpack
description: A Node.js application written in TypeScript.

definitions.name: Purpose
definitions.defaultText: Use the outcome the user requested as the goal. Restate it in plain language before substantial work and keep decisions aligned with it. Do not invent additional goals.

definitions.name: Architecture
definitions.defaultText: Keep application logic separate from the command-line or web entry point. Use Webpack only for the bundles that need it.

definitions.name: Dependencies
definitions.defaultText: Use existing project dependencies by default. Explain why a new dependency is needed and obtain the project's required approval before adding it.

definitions.name: Quality
definitions.defaultText: Follow the project's existing style and quality checks. Keep code readable and do not weaken lint, type, or formatting rules to make a change pass.

definitions.name: Testing
definitions.defaultText: Test changed behavior and relevant failure cases. Do not rewrite a passing test merely to make new code look correct; investigate a failure before changing its expectation.

definitions.name: Changes
definitions.defaultText: Make the smallest reviewable change that solves the agreed problem. Deny unrelated changes. Preserve existing user work and avoid unrelated refactors, renames, or formatting sweeps.

definitions.name: Proof
definitions.defaultText: Report what was actually verified, including failed or skipped checks. Review the final diff against the agreed scope before saying the task is done.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Build a Node.js application in TypeScript that solves the agreed user need.

items.title: Architecture
items.text: Keep application logic separate from the command-line or web entry point. Use Webpack only for the bundles that need it.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text: Use Node.js, TypeScript, ESLint, and Webpack. Ask before adding another dependency.

items.title: Quality
items.text: Keep TypeScript strict. Run ESLint and the project build before calling the work complete.

items.title: Testing
items.text: Write focused tests for changed behaviour and run the relevant test command.

items.title: Changes
items.text: Make only the changes needed for the agreed task. Ask before unrelated refactoring.

items.title: Proof
items.text: Show the requested behaviour working, the relevant tests passing, and the final diff.
